# Maintainer review

Before merging each PR, inspect its final diff and tested commit, including changes by maintainers. Verify the submitting GitHub account matches the folder and each credited profile belongs to the named contributor. Review every specific byline in the workflow and generated README against the actual work; include coauthors where applicable, and confirm that each person agrees to public attribution. Review idea-only or collaborator credit for opt-in with the person concerned. Do not invent names, work or adoption. A correction needs review with affected contributors. Keep the credit record and its readable description when an entry is renamed or retired, as described in CONTRIBUTING.md. Verify the generated README links and run the offline checks.

Review provenance separately for original prose, examples and third-party components, including licenses and required attribution. Check employer authority, material AI-assisted provenance, private or client data, marks and any implication of endorsement. A public issue or discussion does not authorize republication. If evidence is missing or a privacy concern arises, stop the affected merge and refer it to the repository owner without posting sensitive material publicly. Arrange a private exchange for rights evidence. Security vulnerability reports belong in the repository’s Security tab.

Record assent before merging:

1. Link `CLA.md` at the exact base commit using GitHub’s permanent file link. Record the PR number and final reviewed contribution commit.
2. Have the submitter and each additional rights holder confirm from their own GitHub account, or obtain verified authority from a person who can bind a named rights holder. A confirmation can say “I agree to the CLA at [immutable link] for my contribution in PR [number], commit [SHA], and I have authority to grant the stated rights.” Keep sensitive evidence private.
3. Record links to those account-authored confirmations in the PR. Check the signer, agreement version, scope and authority. If the terms, rights holders or covered material change, obtain fresh confirmation for the affected contribution before merge.
4. The automated check sees PR-body checkboxes only. It cannot establish who checked a box, read signatures in comments or verify representation. A maintainer must not check a box or write consent on someone else’s behalf. Pause the merge when consent or authority is uncertain. This manual process documents evidence and does not change the operative agreement.


Preserve original Git commit authors when merging. Use appropriately consented `Co-authored-by: Name <email>` trailers for genuine coauthors, with an email each person agrees to publish, such as their GitHub-provided no-reply address. Never disclose a private email to create attribution. GitHub may recognize contributors when the associated commit email is linked to their account; its contributor graph and recognition are not guaranteed. Check the merge method and resulting history. For squash or rebase, link the final reviewed PR commit to the resulting default-branch commit and verify that the accepted content and intended authors survived. Do not replace specific repository bylines with a contributor graph.

The CI scope and agreement checks are read-only signals, not substitutes for this review. Protect the base workflow, trusted scripts, CODEOWNERS and policy with required owner review and required checks in repository settings. Require branches to be up to date before merging so the generated credits include intervening merges, then rerun the checks. Confirm these protections work for fork PRs. A PR can change its own workflow, so review bootstrap and policy changes manually. Never execute contributor-proposed scripts with privileged credentials, and do not add token writes.
